usa.explanation: "USA" means "the USA". You say "Jeg bor i USA" (I live in the USA), with no word for "the". It is said letter by letter, u-es-a.

sentence.da: New York ligger i **USA**.
sentence.en: New York is in the USA.

uselvisk.explanation: "Uselvisk" means "unselfish", about someone who gives or helps without thinking of their own gain. It is the opposite of "selvisk" (selfish).

sentence.da: Hun er **uselvisk** og hjælper altid andre før sig selv.
sentence.en: She is unselfish and always helps others before herself.

usikker.explanation: "Usikker" means "unsure", not certain. It can also mean "unsafe": "en usikker bro" (an unsafe bridge).

sentence.da: Jeg er **usikker** på, hvad jeg skal sige.
sentence.en: I am unsure what I should say.

uskadt.explanation: "Uskadt" means "unhurt" for a person and "undamaged" for a thing, after something such as an accident, a fall or a storm.

sentence.da: Bilen er helt ødelagt, men føreren er **uskadt**.
sentence.en: The car is completely wrecked, but the driver is unhurt.

uskarp.explanation: "Uskarp" means "blurry" or "out of focus", about things such as a photo, a screen or an edge that is not sharp. The opposite is "skarp" (sharp), which is also used for knives: "en skarp kniv" (a sharp knife).

sentence.da: Min skærm er **uskarp**, så jeg kan ikke læse teksten.
sentence.en: My screen is blurry, so I cannot read the text.

uskyld.explanation: "En uskyld" means "innocence", not having done anything wrong. It also means a childlike lack of experience, as in "børns uskyld" (the innocence of children).

sentence.da: Han kunne bevise sin **uskyld**, og retten løslod ham.
sentence.en: He could prove his innocence, and the court released him.

uskyldig.explanation: "Uskyldig" means "innocent", for a person who did nothing wrong: "Han er uskyldig" (He is innocent). Use it also for something harmless: "Det er en uskyldig joke" (It is an innocent joke).

sentence.da: Dommeren sagde, at han var **uskyldig**.
sentence.en: The judge said that he was innocent.

ustabil.explanation: "Ustabil" means "unstable", for something that wobbles or cannot be trusted to stay as it is. It is the opposite of "stabil" (stable): "Forbindelsen er ustabil" (The connection is unstable).

sentence.da: Stolen er **ustabil**, fordi et ben er kort.
sentence.en: The chair is unstable because one leg is short.

usund.explanation: "Usund" means "unhealthy". It is built from u (un-) and sund (healthy), like "uvenlig" (unfriendly). For example: "usund mad" (unhealthy food).

sentence.da: Slik og kage er **usund** mad.
sentence.en: Candy and cake are unhealthy food.

usympatisk.explanation: "Usympatisk" means "unlikeable", about someone you do not warm to, such as a person who never smiles. Do not mix it up with the English "sympathetic": "sympatisk" means "likeable". To say someone feels for others, use "medfølende" (compassionate): "Hun er medfølende" (She is compassionate).

sentence.da: Manden virkede **usympatisk**, fordi han aldrig smilede.
sentence.en: The man seemed unlikeable because he never smiled.

usynlig.explanation: "Usynlig" means "invisible" and describes something you cannot see. The opposite is "synlig" (visible): "Stjernen er synlig" (The star is visible).

sentence.da: Luften er **usynlig**, men vi trækker vejret.
sentence.en: The air is invisible, but we breathe.

usædvanlig.explanation: "Usædvanlig" means "unusual", for something that does not happen or appear often, so it stands out: "et usædvanligt navn" (an unusual name).

sentence.da: Det er en **usædvanlig** lyd, og jeg kender den ikke.
sentence.en: It is an unusual sound, and I do not know it.

utaknemmelig.explanation: "Utaknemmelig" means "ungrateful", about a person who does not show gratitude. It also describes a job that brings little reward: "en utaknemmelig opgave" (a thankless task).

sentence.da: Han var **utaknemmelig** og sagde aldrig tak for hjælpen.
sentence.en: He was ungrateful and never said thanks for the help.

utallige.explanation: "Utallige" means "countless", so many that you cannot count them: "utallige stjerner" (countless stars). It always goes with more than one thing, so you never put "en" or "et" before it.

sentence.da: Der er **utallige** stjerner på himlen en klar nat.
sentence.en: There are countless stars in the sky on a clear night.

utilfreds.explanation: "Utilfreds" means "dissatisfied". It is the opposite of "tilfreds" (satisfied). To name the thing you are unhappy about, add "med" (with): "Jeg er utilfreds med servicen" (I am dissatisfied with the service).

sentence.da: Kunden er **utilfreds** med maden.
sentence.en: The customer is dissatisfied with the food.

utilfredshed.explanation: "En utilfredshed" means "dissatisfaction", the feeling that something is not as good as it should be: "Der er stor utilfredshed blandt kunderne" (There is great dissatisfaction among the customers).

sentence.da: Der er **utilfredshed** blandt kunderne, fordi leveringen er sen.
sentence.en: There is dissatisfaction among the customers because the delivery is late.

utilstrækkelig.explanation: "Utilstrækkelig" means "inadequate", not enough for what is needed. It also describes a person who feels not good enough: "Jeg føler mig utilstrækkelig" (I feel inadequate). In everyday speech, people often just say "ikke nok" (not enough).

sentence.da: Hjælpen var **utilstrækkelig**, fordi der kun kom én læge.
sentence.en: The help was inadequate because only one doctor came.

utro.explanation: "Utro" means "unfaithful", about a partner who is romantically involved with someone else. It is built from u- (not) and tro (true). To name the person who is betrayed, add "mod" (toward): "Han har været utro mod hende" (He has been unfaithful to her).

sentence.da: Han var **utro**, og hun blev meget ked af det.
sentence.en: He was unfaithful, and she became very sad.

utrolig.explanation: "Utrolig" means "unbelievable", either amazing or hard to believe: "Det er utroligt!" (That is unbelievable!). It is built from at tro (to believe) and u- for the opposite.

sentence.da: Det er en **utrolig** historie, men den er sand.
sentence.en: It is an unbelievable story, but it is true.

utroligt.explanation: "Utroligt" means "incredibly" and makes the next word stronger: "utroligt flot" (incredibly beautiful). Say "Utroligt!" alone when something surprises you, like "wow" in English.

sentence.da: Bjerget er **utroligt** højt.
sentence.en: The mountain is incredibly high.

utydelig.explanation: "Utydelig" means "unclear", hard to see, hear or read: "utydelig skrift" (unclear handwriting).

sentence.da: Hans stemme er **utydelig**, fordi forbindelsen er dårlig.
sentence.en: His voice is unclear because the connection is bad.

utålmodig.explanation: "Utålmodig" means "impatient", describing someone who hates waiting and wants things now. It is the opposite of "tålmodig" (patient).

sentence.da: Jeg er **utålmodig**, for bussen er forsinket.
sentence.en: I am impatient, because the bus is late.

utålmodighed.explanation: "En utålmodighed" means "impatience", the feeling of wanting something to happen faster. Its opposite is "tålmodighed" (patience).

sentence.da: Børnenes **utålmodighed** vokser, fordi bilturen er lang.
sentence.en: The children's impatience grows because the car trip is long.

uundgåelig.explanation: "Uundgåelig" means "inevitable", something that cannot be avoided: "Forsinkelser er uundgåelige" (Delays are inevitable). It is built on "at undgå" (to avoid).

sentence.da: Konflikten var **uundgåelig**, fordi ingen ville give sig.
sentence.en: The conflict was inevitable because no one would give in.

uundværlig.explanation: "Uundværlig" means "indispensable", about a person or thing you cannot do without. It comes from "at undvære" (to do without) and is stronger than "vigtig" (important): without it, things stop working.

sentence.da: Min kaffe er **uundværlig**, når jeg skal op tidligt.
sentence.en: My coffee is indispensable when I have to get up early.

uvant.explanation: "Uvant" means "unfamiliar", about something you are not used to. To name the unfamiliar thing, add "med" (with): "Jeg er uvant med kulden" (I am not used to the cold).

sentence.da: Jeg er **uvant** med at stå op så tidligt.
sentence.en: I am not used to getting up so early.

uvedkommende.explanation: "Uvedkommende" means "irrelevant" about a point that has nothing to do with the matter, and "unauthorized" about people who have no business in a place. The sign "Adgang forbudt for uvedkommende" means "No entry for unauthorized persons".

sentence.da: Det, du siger, er **uvedkommende** for sagen.
sentence.en: What you are saying is irrelevant to the case.

uvenlig.explanation: "Uvenlig" means "unfriendly", and is "venlig" (friendly) with u- in front. To name the person who receives the unfriendly behavior, add "mod" (toward): "Hun var uvenlig mod mig" (She was unfriendly to me).

sentence.da: Han var **uvenlig** og sagde ikke goddag.
sentence.en: He was unfriendly and did not say hello.

uventet.explanation: "Uventet" means "unexpected" and describes something that comes as a surprise.

sentence.da: Besøget var **uventet**, fordi ingen havde ringet.
sentence.en: The visit was unexpected because no one had called.

uvidende.explanation: "Uvidende" means "unaware" or "ignorant", not knowing about something. To name the subject you know nothing about, add "om" (about): "Jeg er uvidende om reglerne" (I am unaware of the rules).

forms.en: a child who does not know

sentence.da: Hun var **uvidende** om planen, fordi ingen havde fortalt hende det.
sentence.en: She was unaware of the plan because no one had told her.

uvidenhed.explanation: "Uvidenhed" means "ignorance", not knowing the facts. To name the subject you know nothing about, add "om" (about): "uvidenhed om reglerne" (ignorance of the rules).

sentence.da: Fejlen skyldtes **uvidenhed**, ikke ond vilje.
sentence.en: The mistake was due to ignorance, not ill will.

uærlig.explanation: "Uærlig" means "dishonest", describing someone who deceives other people. It is built from u- (un-) and ærlig (honest). The prefix u- turns a word into its opposite, as in "uvenlig" (unfriendly).

sentence.da: Han er **uærlig** og snyder tit i spil.
sentence.en: He is dishonest and often cheats at games.

at vaccinere.explanation: "At vaccinere" means "to vaccinate": a doctor or nurse gives you protection so your body can fight a disease. To name the disease, add "mod" (against): "vaccinere mod influenza" (vaccinate against the flu). When you are the person who receives the shot, use "at lade sig vaccinere" (to let yourself be vaccinated): "Jeg lader mig vaccinere" (I am getting vaccinated).

sentence.da: Lægen vil **vaccinere** alle børn i klassen mod mæslinger.
sentence.en: The doctor will vaccinate all the children in the class against measles.

at vade.explanation: "At vade" means "to wade", to walk through water or mud that reaches your legs: "Vi vader ud i havet" (We wade out into the sea). It is also used for walking through deep snow.

sentence.da: Vi kan **vade** over åen, fordi vandet ikke er dybt.
sentence.en: We can wade across the stream because the water is not deep.

at vakle.explanation: "At vakle" means "to wobble" and "to waver". A tired person who walks unsteadily "vakler" (wobbles). About a decision or a belief, it means being unsure and close to changing your mind: "Hans beslutning vakler" (His decision is wavering).

sentence.da: Stolen vil **vakle**, fordi det ene ben er kortere.
sentence.en: The chair will wobble because one leg is shorter.

at vande.explanation: "At vande" means "to water": you give water to plants, flowers and lawns. It is also used for giving animals water to drink: "at vande hestene" (to water the horses). It comes from vand (water).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vande** blomsterne, fordi det ikke har regnet.
sentence.en: I have to water the flowers because it has not rained.

at vandre.explanation: "At vandre" means "to hike" and "to wander". To hike means to go on foot for a long time, often in nature, for the pleasure of it: "Vi vandrer langs kysten hvert efterår" (We hike along the coast every fall). To wander means to walk without hurry or goal: "Han vandrede rundt i byen" (He wandered around town).

sentence.da: Vi vil **vandre** fem timer i bjergene og sove i telt.
sentence.en: We want to hike five hours in the mountains and sleep in a tent.

at vare.explanation: "At vare" means "to last": you say how long something goes on: "Filmen varer to timer" (The movie lasts two hours).

sentence.da: Mødet vil **vare** i cirka en time.
sentence.en: The meeting will last about an hour.

at variere.explanation: "At variere" means "to vary". It works two ways. Something is not always the same: "Prisen varierer" (The price varies). Or you change something on purpose: "Jeg varierer menuen" (I vary the menu).

sentence.da: Temperaturen kan **variere** meget fra dag til dag.
sentence.en: The temperature can vary a lot from day to day.

at vaske.explanation: "At vaske" means "to wash", such as clothes, dishes, your hands or the car. To wash yourself, say "at vaske sig" (to wash oneself). For washing dishes, there is also "at vaske op" (to do the dishes).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vaske** tøjet i dag.
sentence.en: I want to wash the clothes today.

at vaske gulv.explanation: "At vaske gulv" means "to mop the floor" and is said without "gulvet" (the floor): "Vi vasker gulv om lørdagen" (We mop the floor on Saturdays). For one spill, use "at tørre op" (to wipe up).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske gulv**, fordi det er meget beskidt.
sentence.en: I have to mop the floor because it is very dirty.

at vaske op.explanation: "At vaske op" means "to do the dishes" by hand: "Hvem vasker op i dag?" (Who is doing the dishes today?) Do not mix it up with "at vaske" (to wash), which you use for clothes, hands or the car: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske op** efter maden.
sentence.en: I have to do the dishes after the meal.

at vaske sig.explanation: "At vaske sig" means "to wash yourself". The little word "sig" (oneself) becomes "mig" (myself) when you talk about yourself: "jeg vasker mig" (I wash myself). If you wash something else, you drop "sig": "at vaske hænder" (to wash hands) or "at vaske tøj" (to wash clothes).

sentence.da: Han skal **vaske sig** før maden.
sentence.en: He has to wash up before the meal.

at vaske tøj.explanation: "At vaske tøj" means "to do laundry". Literally, it is "to wash clothes". For dishes, say "at vaske op" (to wash the dishes).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske tøj**, fordi jeg ikke har flere rene sokker.
sentence.en: I have to do laundry because I have no more clean socks.

at vedkende sig.explanation: "At vedkende sig" means "to acknowledge", to say openly that something is yours or is true, such as a mistake or a responsibility: "Han vedkender sig sin fejl" (He acknowledges his mistake).

sentence.da: Han har svært ved at **vedkende sig** sine fejl.
sentence.en: He finds it hard to acknowledge his mistakes.

at vedligeholde.explanation: "At vedligeholde" means "to maintain": you keep something in good condition with regular care, such as a house, a garden, a road or a machine: "Vi vedligeholder huset" (We maintain the house). It is not used for claiming something. For that meaning of "maintain", Danes say "at hævde" (to claim).

sentence.da: Man skal **vedligeholde** træværket hvert år, fordi regn skader det.
sentence.en: You must maintain the woodwork every year because rain damages it.

at vedlægge.explanation: "At vedlægge" means "to enclose": you put a document in with a letter, an email or an application: "Jeg vedlægger mit CV" (I enclose my CV). You see it in written Danish. In speech people more often say "at sende med" (to send along).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **vedlægge** mit CV til ansøgningen.
sentence.en: I would like to enclose my résumé with the application.

at vedrøre.explanation: "At vedrøre" means "to concern". You put the person or thing directly after it: "Sagen vedrører dig" (The matter concerns you). Letters and emails often start with "Vedrørende" (Regarding), a form of this word.

sentence.da: Reglen kan **vedrøre** alle elever i skolen.
sentence.en: The rule can concern all students in the school.

at vedtage.explanation: "At vedtage" means "to pass (a law)" or "to adopt": a group officially agrees on something. The group that decides officially, such as a parliament, a council or a board, is the one that passes: "Folketinget vedtog loven" (Parliament passed the law).

sentence.da: Byrådet vil **vedtage** det nye budget i næste uge.
sentence.en: The city council will pass the new budget next week.

at veje.explanation: "At veje" means "to weigh". To state your own weight, use the verb with a number: "Jeg vejer 70 kilo" (I weigh 70 kilos). To measure an object on a scale, name the object after the verb: "Jeg vejer pakken" (I weigh the package).

sentence.da: Man kan **veje** maden på en vægt.
sentence.en: You can weigh the food on a scale.

at vejlede.explanation: "At vejlede" means "to guide" or "to advise", to help someone find the right way with explanations and tips, often as part of a job at a school or an employment office: "Hun vejledte mig i valget" (She advised me on the choice). It is built from vej (way) and lede (lead).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **vejlede** eleverne, når de skriver opgaven.
sentence.en: The teacher will guide the students when they write the assignment.

at veksle.explanation: "At veksle" means "to exchange (money)": you change it from one currency to another. It also means to break a big bill into smaller ones: "Kan du veksle en hundredkroneseddel?" (Can you break a hundred-krone bill?)

sentence.da: Hvor kan jeg **veksle** euro til danske kroner?
sentence.en: Where can I exchange euros for Danish kroner?

at velsigne.explanation: "At velsigne" means "to bless", to ask for good things for someone or to declare something holy, as is done in a church: "Præsten velsigner brudeparret" (The priest blesses the couple). It is built from vel (well) and signe (bless).

sentence.da: Præsten vil **velsigne** parret ved brylluppet.
sentence.en: The priest will bless the couple at the wedding.

at vende.explanation: "At vende" means "to turn" something over or around: "Jeg vender kortet" (I turn the card over). For turning in a direction, say "at dreje" (to turn): "Drej til venstre" (Turn left).

sentence.da: Du kan **vende** siden og læse videre.
sentence.en: You can turn the page and read on.

at vende sig.explanation: "At vende sig" means "to turn around" with your own body: "Han vendte sig og smilede" (He turned around and smiled). Do not mix it up with "at vænne sig til" (to get used to): "Jeg vænner mig til kulden" (I am getting used to the cold).

sentence.da: Han vil **vende sig** og se på mig.
sentence.en: He wants to turn around and look at me.

at vende tilbage.explanation: "At vende tilbage" means "to return": you come back to a place or a topic: "Han vender tilbage til byen" (He returns to the city). It is also a polite way to say you will answer later: "Jeg vender tilbage til dig" (I will get back to you).

sentence.da: Vi vil **vende tilbage** til Danmark næste år.
sentence.en: We want to return to Denmark next year.

at vente.explanation: "At vente" means "to wait": "Jeg venter på bussen" (I am waiting for the bus). It can also mean "to expect": "Hun venter barn" (She is expecting a baby).

sentence.da: Børn kan ikke **vente** til jul.
sentence.en: Kids cannot wait for Christmas.

at vente på.explanation: "At vente på" means "to wait for" someone or something. The small word "på" (for) stays at the end of a question: "Hvem venter du på?" (Who are you waiting for?)

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vente på** bussen.
sentence.en: I have to wait for the bus.

at verificere.explanation: "At verificere" means "to verify": you make sure that something is true or correct, such as who a person is. Banks and websites use it for identity: "at verificere sin identitet" (to verify your identity).

sentence.da: Journalisten vil **verificere** kilderne, fordi nyheden kan være falsk.
sentence.en: The journalist wants to verify the sources because the news may be false.

at vide.explanation: "At vide" means "to know" a fact: "Jeg ved det ikke" (I do not know). For knowing a person or a place, Danish uses a different word, "at kende" (to know someone): "Jeg kender Anna" (I know Anna).

sentence.da: Du skal **vide** dit telefonnummer.
sentence.en: You need to know your phone number.

at videreføre.explanation: "At videreføre" means "to continue", in the sense of carrying on something that already exists, such as a tradition or a project that others began. For simply keeping going, say "at fortsætte" (to continue): "Jeg fortsætter med at læse" (I keep on reading).

sentence.da: Hun vil **videreføre** familiens firma, når hendes far går på pension.
sentence.en: She wants to carry on the family business when her father retires.

at videregive.explanation: "At videregive" means "to pass on", to give information or an object on to another person: "Jeg videregiver beskeden til chefen" (I pass the message on to the boss).

sentence.da: Lægen må ikke **videregive** dine oplysninger til andre.
sentence.en: The doctor may not pass on your information to others.

at vidne.explanation: "At vidne" means "to testify": you tell a court what you saw or know. The same word also names the person: "et vidne" (a witness). With "om" (about) it means "to show": "Resultatet vidner om hårdt arbejde" (The result shows hard work).

sentence.da: Hun skal **vidne** i retten, fordi hun så ulykken.
sentence.en: She must testify in court because she saw the accident.

at vifte.explanation: "At vifte" means "to wave" something back and forth, usually with "med" (with): "Han vifter med en avis" (He waves a newspaper). To wave to a person, use "at vinke" (to wave to someone) instead. The noun "en vifte" means "a fan".

sentence.da: Børnene skal **vifte** med små flag, når kongen kommer.
sentence.en: The children will wave small flags when the king comes.

at ville.explanation: "At ville" means "to want to": "Jeg vil have en kop kaffe" (I want a cup of coffee). Adding "gerne" (gladly) makes it polite: "Jeg vil gerne have en kop kaffe" (I would like a cup of coffee). For a duty, use "skal" (have to) instead: "Jeg skal gå" (I have to go).

sentence.da: Børn kan altid **ville** have mere.
sentence.en: Kids can always want more.

at vinde.explanation: "At vinde" means "to win". The one who wins is "en vinder" (a winner).

sentence.da: Holdet med flest mål vil **vinde** kampen.
sentence.en: The team with the most goals will win the match.

at vinke.explanation: "At vinke" means "to wave" your hand. Name the person you wave at with "til" (to): "Han vinkede til mig" (He waved to me). To wave goodbye, add "farvel" (goodbye): "Han vinkede farvel" (He waved goodbye).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vinke** til dig, når toget kører.
sentence.en: I will wave to you when the train leaves.

at vippe.explanation: "At vippe" means "to tip" or "to rock": you move up on one side and down on the other. "En vippe" is a seesaw, and "Vip ikke med stolen!" (Do not rock the chair!) is said to children who lean back.

sentence.da: Hvis bordet står skævt, kan det **vippe**.
sentence.en: If the table stands crooked, it can rock.

at virke.explanation: "At virke" means "to work" and also "to seem". To work means that something functions: "Bilen virker ikke" (The car does not work). To seem means that something gives a certain impression: "Han virker træt" (He seems tired).

sentence.da: Telefonen vil ikke **virke** i dag.
sentence.en: The phone won't work today.

at vise.explanation: "At vise" means "to show": "Jeg viser billedet" (I show the picture). Danish needs no "til" (to) here: "Hun viser mig bogen" (She shows me the book).

sentence.da: Kan du **vise** mig vej?
sentence.en: Can you show me the way?

at vise sig.explanation: "At vise sig" means "to turn out": you find out how a person or situation really is. To name what the person turned out to be, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Hun viste sig at være meget flink" (She turned out to be very nice).

sentence.da: Det kan **vise sig**, at han har ret.
sentence.en: It may turn out that he is right.

at visne.explanation: "At visne" means "to wither": a plant dries up and goes limp because it lacks water or is dying. Danes also use it for something fading away, such as a smile: "Smilet visnede" (The smile faded).

sentence.da: Blomsterne vil **visne**, når du glemmer at vande dem.
sentence.en: The flowers will wither when you forget to water them.

at visualisere.explanation: "At visualisere" means "to visualize", to picture something in your mind or to show information as a drawing or graph.

sentence.da: Vi bruger et diagram til at **visualisere** tallene.
sentence.en: We use a chart to visualize the figures.

at vokse.explanation: "At vokse" means "to grow", for anything that gets bigger, such as children, plants and things: "Børn vokser hurtigt" (Children grow fast). To grow up is "at vokse op": "Jeg voksede op i Odense" (I grew up in Odense). To grow tomatoes, use "at dyrke" (to cultivate).

sentence.da: Planterne kan **vokse** meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: The plants can grow very fast.

at vokse op.explanation: "At vokse op" means "to grow up": you spend your childhood somewhere. Without "op" (up), "at vokse" means "to grow", for example for plants: "Træet vokser hurtigt" (The tree grows quickly).

sentence.da: Mine børn skal **vokse op** på landet.
sentence.en: My children will grow up in the countryside.

at vove.explanation: "At vove" means "to dare": you do something even though it might go wrong. In everyday speech Danes mostly say "at turde" (to dare): "Jeg tør ikke" (I do not dare).

sentence.da: Ingen vil **vove** at gå ind i det mørke hus.
sentence.en: No one will dare to go into the dark house.

at vride.explanation: "At vride" means "to twist" or "to wring": you turn something hard with your hands, often to squeeze the water out. With "sig" (oneself) it means "to writhe": "Han vred sig af smerte" (He writhed in pain).

sentence.da: Du skal **vride** vandet ud af håndklædet.
sentence.en: You must wring the water out of the towel.

at vrimle.explanation: "At vrimle" means "to swarm" or "to teem": a place is full of many small things moving about, such as people or insects. It is followed by "med" (with): "Gaden vrimler med mennesker" (The street teems with people).

sentence.da: Om sommeren kan stranden **vrimle** med børn og turister.
sentence.en: In the summer, the beach can swarm with children and tourists.

at vurdere.explanation: "At vurdere" means "to evaluate": you form an opinion about how good, big or valuable something is. It is also used for setting a price: "Huset bliver vurderet til tre millioner" (The house is valued at three million).

sentence.da: Lægen skal **vurdere**, om skaden er alvorlig.
sentence.en: The doctor must assess whether the injury is serious.

at vågne.explanation: "At vågne" means "to wake up" by yourself. When someone else wakes you, Danish uses "at vække" (to wake someone).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vågne** klokken syv.
sentence.en: I have to wake up at seven.

at vågne op.explanation: "At vågne op" means "to wake up", the moment you become awake. People often just say "at vågne" (to wake up), so "op" (up) is optional.

sentence.da: Jeg plejer at **vågne op** klokken seks.
sentence.en: I usually wake up at six.

at vædde.explanation: "At vædde" means "to bet". To name the event you bet on, use "på" (on): "Vi vædder på vejret" (We bet on the weather).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vædde** på, at holdet vinder i aften.
sentence.en: I will bet that the team wins tonight.

at vække.explanation: "At vække" means "to wake someone": "Jeg vækker børnene" (I wake the children). To wake up yourself, say "at vågne" (to wake up): "Jeg vågnede tidligt" (I woke up early).

sentence.da: Kan du **vække** mig klokken seks?
sentence.en: Can you wake me at six?

at vælge.explanation: "At vælge" means "to choose" or "to pick". "Et valg" means both "a choice" and "an election".

sentence.da: Du må **vælge** rød eller blå.
sentence.en: You may choose red or blue.

at vælte.explanation: "At vælte" means "to knock over" and "to tip over": "Jeg vælter koppen" (I knock over the cup). Something can also go over by itself: "Træet væltede" (The tree fell over).

forms.en: I have knocked over / tipped over

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **vælte** glasset!
sentence.en: Be careful, you might knock over the glass!

at vænne sig af med.explanation: "At vænne sig af med" means "to get out of the habit of": you stop doing something you used to do regularly: "Han vænnede sig af med at ryge" (He got out of the habit of smoking). It is the opposite of "at vænne sig til" (to get used to).

forms.en: to get out of the habit of
I get out of the habit of
I got out of the habit of

forms.da: jeg har vænnet mig af med
forms.en: I have gotten out of the habit of

sentence.da: Han vil **vænne sig af med** at spise sukker hver dag.
sentence.en: He wants to get out of the habit of eating sugar every day.

at vænne sig til.explanation: "At vænne sig til" means "to get used to": you slowly become used to something. To say you are already used to it, use "vant til" (used to): "Jeg er vant til kulden" (I am used to the cold).

sentence.da: Det tager tid at **vænne sig til** et nyt sted.
sentence.en: It takes time to get used to a new place.

at værdsætte.explanation: "At værdsætte" means "to appreciate": you value something and are glad of it: "Jeg værdsætter din hjælp" (I appreciate your help). It never means to go up in value, as it can in English. For that, say "at stige i værdi" (to rise in value).

sentence.da: Man skal kunne **værdsætte** de små ting i livet.
sentence.en: You have to be able to appreciate the small things in life.

at være.explanation: "At være" means "to be": "Jeg er glad" (I am happy). The form "er" (am, is, are) is the same for everyone: "jeg er" (I am), "han er" (he is), "vi er" (we are).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **være** hjemme i dag.
sentence.en: I want to be at home today.

at være bange for.explanation: "At være bange for" means "to be afraid of". To name the action you fear, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Jeg er bange for at falde" (I am afraid of falling).

sentence.da: Børn kan **være bange for** mørket.
sentence.en: Children can be afraid of the dark.

at være enig.explanation: "At være enig" means "to agree" and literally says "to be in agreement": "Jeg er enig med dig" (I agree with you). To name the topic you agree on, add "i" (in): "Vi er enige i det" (We agree on that).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **være enig** i det.
sentence.en: I can agree with that.

at være i tvivl.explanation: "At være i tvivl" means "to be in doubt" or "to be unsure": "Jeg er i tvivl om svaret" (I am unsure about the answer).

sentence.da: Når man ikke ved svaret, kan man **være i tvivl**.
sentence.en: When you do not know the answer, you can be in doubt.

at være kærester.explanation: "At være kærester" means "to be dating" or "to be a couple". One person in the couple is "en kæreste" (a boyfriend or girlfriend).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **være kærester** med dig.
sentence.en: I would like us to be a couple.

at være med.explanation: "At være med" means "to take part": you join what others are doing: "Er du med?" (Are you in?) It also means "to follow along": "Jeg er ikke helt med" (I am not quite following).

forms.en: to take part / be in on it

sentence.da: Vil du **være med**, når vi spiller fodbold?
sentence.en: Do you want to join in when we play soccer?

at være nødt til.explanation: "At være nødt til" means "to have to", when you have no other choice: "Jeg er nødt til at gå nu" (I have to go now). It is stronger than "skal" (must, am going to), which can be just a plan: "Jeg skal på arbejde" (I am going to work).

sentence.da: Hvis bussen er væk, kan vi **være nødt til** at gå.
sentence.en: If the bus is gone, we may have to walk.

at være oppe at køre.explanation: "At være oppe at køre" means "to be worked up", to be tense, excited and full of restless energy: "Han er helt oppe at køre før eksamen" (He is all worked up before the exam).

forms.da: Han var oppe at køre i går
Vær ikke så oppe at køre
forms.en: Do not be so worked up

sentence.da: Han plejer at **være oppe at køre**, når der er eksamen.
sentence.en: He tends to be worked up when there is an exam.

at være på bar bund.explanation: "At være på bar bund" means "to be at a total loss": you have no idea what to do or answer, with nothing to build on. Literally, it is "to be on bare bottom".

forms.en: I am at a total loss
She was at a total loss
We are at a total loss

sentence.da: Han vil **være på bar bund** til eksamen, fordi han ikke har læst.
sentence.en: He will be at a total loss at the exam because he has not studied.

at være på herrens mark.explanation: "At være på Herrens mark" means "to be completely lost": you are totally confused or wrong about something: "Der er du helt på Herrens mark" (You are completely off there). Literally, it is "to be on the Lord's field".

forms.da: Jeg er helt på Herrens mark
Vi var helt på Herrens mark

related.da: at være helt ude at svømme
related.en: to be out of your depth
to be on the right track

sentence.da: Han kan **være på Herrens mark**, når han ikke har læst opgaven.
sentence.en: He can be completely lost when he has not read the assignment.

at være på vej.explanation: "At være på vej" means "to be on the way": "Jeg er på vej hjem" (I am on my way home). To name the place you are heading to, add "til" (to): "Han er på vej til Aarhus" (He is on his way to Aarhus).

forms.en: I have been on my way

sentence.da: Vi skal **være på vej** inden otte.
sentence.en: We must be on our way before eight.

at være syg.explanation: "At være syg" means "to be sick" or "to be ill": "Jeg er syg" (I am sick). To get sick, say "at blive syg" (to become sick): "Jeg bliver syg" (I am getting sick).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **være syg** i ferien.
sentence.en: I do not want to be sick on vacation.
